title.title: The Abhyankar–Sathaye conjecture fails in four variables
title.subtitle: Claim: an explicit $F$ in $\mathbb{C}[h,u,v,w]$ whose zero set is $\mathbb{C}^3$, yet $F$ is not a coordinate

plain: A slice of 4D space that is itself flat 3D space, yet can't be straightened into a coordinate slice

beats.text: Perturb the cusp $(u^3,-u^2)$; the zero set of $F$ is a copy of affine 3-space
Expanded, $F$ has 69 terms and degree 17, and its gradient vanishes at one point
So no automorphism sends a variable to $F$

steps: Its zero set is a copy of ordinary 3-space: the hard half
But at one point all four slopes of F vanish; a coordinate's never do
So no change of variables turns F into a variable

data.label: $\nabla F = 0$ here
data.caption: a coordinate's gradient is never zero

achievement.label: Abhyankar–Sathaye embedding conjecture (1970s)
achievement.context: Before: true for lines in the plane (Abhyankar–Moh–Suzuki); open for $n \ge 3$ for fifty years
achievement.note: Every $n \ge 4$; the original question in three variables is untouched

verify.detail: Lean: $\mathbb{C}[x]/(F) \cong \mathbb{C}^{[n-1]}$ and no automorphism sends a variable to $F$
verify.ourCheck: We expanded $F$ exactly and found $\nabla F = 0$; we did not build the Lean

voice.text: Its zero set is affine three-space, yet the polynomial is not a coordinate.
At one point, all four slopes vanish, which no coordinate allows.
Claimed: a counterexample in every dimension from four.
